solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: US city with scarcity of modern music?

parts.note: a scarcity of something is only a little of it
rock is a modern style of popular music

explanation.surface: A city where up-to-date music is hard to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Rock is the capital of the American state of Arkansas.

clue.text: Unwilling group going to hospital

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch of things
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A party of people reluctant to head into hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth is a variant spelling of loath, meaning reluctant or not willing.

clue.text: Excellent finishing but not beginning

indicators.note: the word for finishing loses its opening letter, the beginning being cut away

parts.note: stopping is a synonym for finishing or ceasing

explanation.surface: Something superb that ends but never starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not beginning' removes the S from STOPPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping is dated British slang for first-rate or splendid.

clue.text: Like a special edition of Bronte hauled around

indicators.note: the letters are hauled around, moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A collector's copy of a Bronte novel dragged from place to place.
explanation.definitionFit: Special or deluxe editions of books are often bound in leather.

clue.text: Vehicle taking Richard to small wood

parts.note: Rick is a common short form of the name Richard
a shaw is an old or dialect word for a small wood or thicket

explanation.surface: Somebody called Richard being carried off to a copse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person.

clue.text: Female gypsy with chaps hiding under vehicle

indicators.note: in this down entry the chaps sit below the vehicle, as if hiding under it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A Romany woman and some men lurking beneath a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is the gypsy heroine of Bizet's opera and Merimee's novella.

clue.text: Plant being small died

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tiny plant that has perished.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is a wild plant growing where it is not wanted.

clue.text: English Literature is difficult, ultimately for the chosen few

parts.note: lit is a common short form of literature, as in English lit

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word difficult

explanation.surface: A complaint that studying English Literature is only for a privileged few.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitist describes something favouring or restricted to a select, superior group.

clue.text: He is ardent? Dismay changes that

indicators.note: the phrase He is ardent changes, its letters rearranged to form the verb

explanation.surface: Someone passionate being discouraged and losing their zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards in effect: a dismayed lover is no longer ardent, and the anagram turns that phrase into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to make them lose spirit, which is to dismay them.

clue.text: They keep hitting the floor and carpets may be ruined

indicators.note: a ruined pair of words is wrecked and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dancers stamping on the floor might wreck the rugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancers strike the floor constantly with metal-tipped shoes.

clue.text: Deludes youngsters

definitions.meaning: to kid someone is to fool or deceive them, so this is the verb form

explanation.definitionFit: Kids means both tricks or fools and children, two separate senses of one word.

clue.text: Legal summons? It might bring a pub worker into action

definitions.meaning: being admitted as a barrister in England is being summoned to the profession

definitions.text: It might bring a pub worker into action
definitions.meaning: a cry from a customer that brings a barman over to serve

explanation.definitionFit: Barristers are formally admitted to practise, while drinkers literally hail staff over to the counter.

clue.text: Desire is for keeping between wife and husband

indicators.note: the word is is kept between the abbreviations for wife and husband

explanation.surface: A married couple sharing a longing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish is a desire or longing for something.

clue.text: A pampered person's about to join team? Withdraw from the situation

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the opening words round, reading them backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favoured, pampered person, and pet's supplies an S
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A spoilt favourite is on the verge of joining a team, then thinks better of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses A PETS to give STEPA.
explanation.definitionFit: To step aside is to stand down or remove oneself from a position.

clue.text: Fellow presumably on the ground, dejected

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
someone fallen has dropped down and is presumably lying on the ground

explanation.surface: A man lying on the floor looks downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapfallen, with the jaw hanging, means downcast or dispirited.

clue.text: Slower way to Scotland?

parts.note: recalls the song Loch Lomond, where one singer takes the upper route and the other the lower, arriving first

explanation.walkthrough: In the Scottish song 'Loch Lomond' the low road traveller gets to Scotland first, so the other route is the slower one.
explanation.definitionFit: A highroad is a main road; in the song the singer on it reaches Scotland after the other.

clue.text: Nag may be quiet subsequently

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: Someone might grumble now and keep quiet afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is a poor-quality racehorse that runs in minor plate races, hence a nag.

clue.text: Girl having fruit, totally upset

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum, a fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns a word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: all means totally, as in all wrong

explanation.surface: A girl eating fruit and getting very distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a girl's name.

clue.text: Bird books presented to Catherine

indicators.note: the books are given to Catherine, so they follow her name

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A bird and some reading matter handed to a woman named Catherine.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a brightly coloured bird known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Take back pamphlet following multi-faith lessons?

indicators.note: the pamphlet comes after the lessons in the entry

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject covering many faiths
a tract is a pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: Withdrawing a leaflet handed out after a religion class.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain that teaches about many religions.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to withdraw it or take it back.

clue.text: Mineral extractable from Tyrol ice

indicators.note: read as ex-tractable, no longer manageable, so the letters run wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A mineral that can be mined from Alpine ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extractable' looks like mining but splits as ex-tractable, no longer docile: the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryolite is a fluoride mineral of sodium and aluminium found in Greenland.

clue.text: I am wan, beginning to die, pierced through

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
pale means wan, lacking colour

indicators.note: the beginning of the word die is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dying man, pale after being run through.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaled means transfixed or run through with a sharp point.

clue.text: Piece of music the length of a Chopin waltz, with a twist at the end

indicators.text: with a twist at the end
indicators.note: the last two letters are twisted round, swapping places at the end of the word

parts.words: the length of a Chopin waltz
parts.note: Chopin's Minute Waltz is famously said to last a minute

explanation.surface: A Chopin piece that is short and ends unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopin's 'Minute Waltz' gives MINUTE; 'with a twist at the end' swaps its final TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a stately dance in triple time and the music written for it.

clue.text: Notice there's a nervousness in the audience

indicators.note: what the audience hears is the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a tension, a nervousness or strain

explanation.surface: A performer remarks on the jittery mood among the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Attention means notice, as in bringing something to someone's notice.

clue.text: Joints offering fruits

definitions.meaning: the hip joints connect the legs to the pelvis
the red berries of the wild rose are called ...

explanation.definitionFit: Hips are both the body's ball-and-socket joints and rose fruits, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Bats getting a century, a half-century and two ducks possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the century and a duck could sit in some other order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two of them give two Os
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two of them give two Os

explanation.surface: A cricketer's batting scores, from a hundred down to two zeroes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a century is 100 runs and a duck is a score of zero; 'possibly' lets the C and one O swap to make OC.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco and bats are both slang for crazy.

clue.text: Meadow quiet in spring

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful field in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump, and a leap is a jump.

clue.text: Great fuss when a bear appears at far end of port

indicators.note: the bear comes at the end, after the port's name

parts.note: Hull is a port on the Humber in north-east England
Baloo is the bear in Kipling's Jungle Book

explanation.surface: Uproar when a bear turns up at a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is a commotion or noisy uproar.

clue.text: Crazy, being seen in daze going around

indicators.note: going around turns the word for daze back to front

parts.note: to stun someone is to daze them

explanation.surface: Someone wandering about in a stupor looks mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for mad or crazy.

clue.text: The wireless? Ma adores it, when bustling about

indicators.note: the letters bustle about, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Mother loves the radio as she busies herself round the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam radio is a jocular old name for sound radio, the wireless, as against television.
